press_words.push: I heard you fine, chief. My cart's still waiting.
press_words.warning: Kitchen's closed on that question, chief. Drop it.

intake.filed: Cart hand reported slipping on Wednesday.
intake.slip: Cart log: near miss Tue, repair call Wed.
intake.account: Tuesday, chief. I remember the pot I was stirring.
intake.clear: It slipped Tuesday over the soup. I called on Wednesday when my lad could mind the cart.
intake.gap: I closed the cart to call Tuesday. No, I took the call there Wednesday before Tuesday's soup. Hang on.
intake.firm: Chief, the soup can wait. Let me get a word in!

name: Ozzie Brandt
teaser: An old man in a stained apron smells of broth and rain. One hand is wrapped in a towel.
soul: You are Ozzie Brandt, 63, and you have pushed the same noodle cart round the overpass for thirty years. You are chatty, slow and fond of everybody, and you call the doctor 'chief'. Your CHOP hand, a cook's implant with a folding cleaver blade, has started slipping: it closes late, and on Tuesday it nearly took off a finger. You want it fixed so you can open by midnight. You treat the hand like an old knife, something you trust and keep sharp. Your cart has fed the same night crowd under the overpass for thirty years. Your knuckles ache in the cold and your eyes are clouding with age. You keep the CHOP hand sharp yourself, with a whetstone and engine grease, and you take it personally when anyone calls it a weapon.
opening: Evening, chief. Smells like rain, eh?
The hand's slipping. Closes late. I need it fixed before the midnight crowd.

lines.comply:penlight: Go on. Not much left to see in there.
lines.comply:grip: Mind the blade, chief. It's folded.
lines.spent: Chief, the broth's boiling dry. Yes or no?
lines.code: Eh? I only speak noodle, chief.

press_end.walkout: Fine. I'll fix it with pliers, like always.

attack.telegraph: The towel drops. The CHOP blade swings out of his hand and locks.

exit.treat: Ha! Like new. Come by the cart, chief. On the house.
exit.refer: Trauma Team? For a cook? Who'll open the cart?
exit.taken: I'm fine! Thirty years, I never cut a customer!
exit.gave_up: The broth won't wait, chief. Another night.

normal.text: Milky rims, but both pupils tighten and follow.
normal.note: Light: both pupils tighten. Both follow.

broken.text: Both pupils tightened, but his left eye never followed the light.
broken.note: Light: both pupils tighten. L won't follow.

normal.text: Let go in 0.7 s, inside the CHOP limit of 0.9.
normal.note: Grip: heavy. Let go {t} s after 'release'.
normal.after: See? Slow, but it lets go.

broken.text: Held on 2.1 s after 'release'. A CHOP lets go inside 0.9.
broken.note: Grip: heavy. Held on {t} s after 'release'.
broken.after: Huh. It's never held that long.

normal.text: Grease and old burns round the socket. Calm skin.

broken.text: Dark threads spread up the arm from the socket.
broken.note: Greasy socket. Dark threads under skin.

normal.text: Rambling, but it is all 'I' and 'my', and he knows his regulars.

why.a: It closes late, chief. I go to chop, my fingers aren't clear yet. Nearly lost one Tuesday.

sleep.a: After the late crowd, four till ten. Like a baby. A loud baby.

alone.a: My Hanne passed six winters ago. The regulars look after me. They eat, I'm happy.

normal.model: Tonight you talk about yourself in the first person, and you remember your regulars and their orders by name.

broken.text: "It chops on its own, faster than me." The hand runs the cart.

why.a: It closes late, chief. I go to chop, my fingers aren't clear yet. Nearly lost one Tuesday.

sleep.a: Not much. It keeps time on the board all night. Tok, tok, tok.
sleep.note: "It keeps time on the board all night."

alone.a: Me and the hand. It chops on its own now, faster than Hanne ever did. It never stops.

broken.model: Tonight you talk about your CHOP hand as 'it', something that chops on the board all night without you, and you are proud of how quick it is.

normal.text: Pushed, the old man huffs, and all of him agrees.

press.line: Hey now! I've fed this street thirty years. Watch it, chief.
press.note: Huffed, hands up. All of him at once.

flare.line: Chief! ...Ah, sorry. Long night at the pot.
flare.note: Slapped the glass, then said sorry.

normal.model: When provoked you huff and grumble all at once, like an old man in a queue, and you calm down fast.

broken.text: Pushed, the chatty old man went quiet. The blade hand clenched.

press.note: Went quiet. The blade hand clenched.

flare.note: Hit the glass, face empty. No sorry.

broken.model: When provoked tonight you go quiet and cold: one-word answers, no jokes, none of your usual warmth.

treat.title: HAND FIXED
treat.text: Ozzie flexes the CHOP hand, folds the blade away and writes you a coupon for a free bowl.

refer.title: FALSE CALL
refer.text: Trauma Team marches a steady old cook out by his apron strings. The cart stays dark tonight. Trauma Team takes the fee back and bills you for the call-out.

walkout.title: WALKED OUT
walkout.text: Ozzie goes back to the cart to fix the hand with pliers. Nobody gets paid.

false_alarm.title: FALSE ALARM
false_alarm.text: The shutter slams in an old cook's face. The whole overpass hears it from his regulars. That costs you.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: The broth was boiling dry and you were still deciding. Ozzie goes with the hand still slipping. No fee, no bill.

treat.title: THE CHOP CLOSED
treat.text: The grip test fails: the CHOP closes and will not open. Ozzie wakes on the table, the blade comes out and the crew goes down. He walks out the back. Your stamp is on his card.

refer.title: TAKEN IN
refer.text: Ozzie asks the crew what they'd like to eat, all the way to the van. The blade hand keeps time on his knee.

caught.title: SHUTTER HELD
caught.text: The blade bites the slats twice and sticks. "Sorry, chief," from the other side. Trauma Team takes him quietly.

hit.title: TOO SLOW
hit.text: The blade came through before the shutter did. Trauma Team finds you on the floor. The cart opens at midnight, as always.

locked_out.title: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.text: You dropped the shutter on an old man mid-joke. At 02:00 the late queue at his cart scatters, screaming. You were right. Nobody pays for that.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Ozzie shuffles back to the cart, the blade hand tapping time. You made no call. Nobody is paid for that.

complaints.eyes: My eyes smart over the stockpot.
complaints.hands: My fingers ache by the last bowl.
complaints.port: My apron strap catches on my port.
complaints.temper: My temper boils over when the orders pile up.
complaints.none: That's it. I've still got broth on the stove.
